title: Pro Vice Chancellor — Administration
content: The Pro-Vice Chancellor acts as Vice Chancellor when the regular VC is on leave, abroad, or the position is vacant.

content: The Registrar is a full-time officer and custodian of the university seal. They handle general administration, academic matters, and staff establishment.

title: Treasurer — Administration

title: Hostel — Administration

title: First Women University — History
content: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University Peshawar is the first public sector women university in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

title: Benazir Bhutto — History
content: The university was named to honor Benazir Bhutto and other women of Pakistan who contributed to women empowerment and national development.

title: Inauguration — History
content: The campus was inaugurated on 1 September 2004 by the Chief Minister of KPK.

title: Law — History
content: The university was established under the Frontier Women University Act 2004, later published in 2005 as a provincial act.

title: Vice Chancellor — History
content: The first Vice Chancellor, Prof. Dr. Syeda Farhana Jahangir, was appointed on 10 June 2005.

title: Camp Office — History
content: The university initially operated from the Department of Psychology at the University of Peshawar and became functional in a college hostel building.

title: Departments — History
content: In February 2006, academic activities started with 8 departments including Arabic, Psychology, Computer Science, Islamiat, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, and English with 240 students.

title: Infrastructure — History
content: In 2007, land of 400 kanals was allotted but initially occupied, and a PC-I project worth 456 million rupees was approved.

title: New Programs — History
content: New disciplines like Bioinformatics and Microbiology were introduced in 2007 along with a Clinical Psychology diploma and psychotherapeutic clinic.

title: Women Development — History
content: Women Development Center and Education Department were established in 2008, introducing B.Ed, diplomas, and certificate programs.

title: Mphil Phd — History
content: MPhil and PhD programs started in English, Islamiat, and Psychology. Several colleges were affiliated and international MoUs were signed with UK universities.

title: Disciplines — History
content: In 2010, new disciplines like Law, Political Science, Urdu, Management Sciences, and Art & Design were introduced.

title: Renaming — History
content: The university was renamed from Frontier Women University to Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University through a legal amendment in 2010.

title: Higher Studies — History
content: In 2012, MS programs and MPhil leading to PhD in Economics, Computer Science, and Management Sciences were introduced under the KPK Universities Act 2012.

title: Growth — History
content: By 2012, the university had 4600 students in 18 departments and 16 affiliated colleges with over 5000 students.

title: Infrastructure — History
content: The university built academic blocks, hostels, administration block, and IT infrastructure including a high-speed network and wireless system.

title: Ranking — History
content: The university was ranked 9th by HEC among 27 new universities in Pakistan despite security and infrastructure challenges.

title: Education — Overview
content: Education is essential for national development and economic growth. Increasing literacy rate is key for reducing poverty.

title: Pakistan — Overview
content: Pakistan invests in education to improve human resources and economic productivity through skill development.

title: Mission — Overview
content: The university aims to provide quality education to women across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including remote areas.

title: Student Development — Overview
content: The institution focuses on academic, moral, physical, professional, and spiritual development of students.

title: Expansion — Overview
content: The university has expanded disciplines continuously since 2005 and remains the largest provider of female education in KPK.

title: Facilities — Overview
content: Modern facilities include IT centers, research units, accommodation near campus, and industry-linked programs for employability.

title: Eligibility — Hostel Admission
content: Hostel accommodation is limited and not guaranteed. Students within 20 km of Peshawar are not eligible. Admission to university does not ensure hostel allotment and is subject to availability for regular students only.

title: Merit — Hostel Admission
content: Hostel admission is merit-based, renewed every semester, and seats are allocated proportionally to institutions. Outstation students are given priority, while local students may be considered with valid relocation proof.

title: Application — Hostel Process
content: Students must apply through their institution using the prescribed form with photographs obtained from the Provost Office. Admission requires approval and compliance with university procedures.

title: Research Students — Hostel Research
content: Research students must be full-time and may require NOC and study leave if employed. Hostel tenure for research programs is up to two years and three months including extension.

title: Dues — Hostel Finance
content: Hostel dues are set by university rules and managed under the Provost Office, which supervises hostel admissions and student affairs.

title: Closure — Hostel Rules
content: Hostels may close during vacations or administrative decisions. Residents must vacate when required and follow all official instructions.

title: Timings — Hostel Routine
content: Hostel routine includes study hours (winter 8–10 pm, summer 9–11 pm), fixed gate timings, and scheduled morning/evening shifts for university commute.

title: Security — Hostel Visitors
content: Strict visitor rules apply: male visitors are not allowed inside. Female guests require warden approval. Only parents/guardians may visit under defined timings and conditions.

title: Leave — Hostel Discipline
content: All leave requests, complaints, and permissions must go through the warden. Residents must follow sign-out procedures and maintain proper leave records.

title: Monitoring — Hostel Monitoring
content: Residents are monitored through attendance checks, room inspections, and must follow discipline rules including return-time logging and cleanliness standards.

content: provost office contact information is +093456601.

title: Library — Library Overview
content: The Central Library of Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University was established in 2006 and moved to its purpose-built building in 2014. It supports academic and research needs with over 13,000 volumes including books, journals, magazines, theses, and research papers.

title: Library — Digital Services
content: The library provides Web OPAC for online catalog search and access to HEC Digital Library resources for students and faculty.

title: Library — Library Structure
content: Library sections include Acquisition, Reading Room, Circulation, Reference & Journals, Research and IT Lab, Eleanor Roosevelt Corner, and Technical Services.

title: Library — Library System
content: Books are organized using the Dewey Decimal Classification system, where each item is assigned a unique call number based on its subject to help locate it on shelves.

title: Library — Library Services
content: Library services include borrowing books, reference assistance, and reader advisory support to help users access and utilize library resources effectively.

title: Library — Library Timing
content: Library operates Monday to Friday from 08:30 AM to 03:15 PM. Circulation timing is from 09:30 AM to 02:00 PM. The library remains closed on public holidays.

title: Library — Library Rules
content: Library rules include maintaining silence, no eating or drinking, proper handling of books, returning materials on time, and reporting lost library cards immediately.

content: Library contact information: Email librarian@sbbwu.edu.pk and phone +92-91-9224749 for inquiries and support.

title: Passing Marks — Passing Rules
content: A student must obtain at least 50% marks in each paper to pass.

title: Grade A — Grading
content: 85% and above corresponds to Grade A with GPA 4.0 and Excellent performance.

title: Grade B — Grading
content: 70 to 84% corresponds to Grade B with GPA between 3.0 and 3.9.

title: Grade C — Grading
content: 60 to 69% corresponds to Grade C with GPA between 2.0 and 2.9.

title: Grade D — Grading
content: 50 to 59% corresponds to Grade D with GPA between 1.0 and 1.9.

title: Fail — Grading
content: Marks below 50% correspond to Grade F which means fail.

title: Withdrawn — Grading
content: Grade W indicates a withdrawn course.

title: Incomplete — Grading
content: Grade I indicates an incomplete course.

title: Sgpa — Gpa
content: SGPA is calculated by dividing the sum of grade points multiplied by credit hours by total credit hours in a semester.

title: Cgpa — Gpa
content: CGPA is calculated by dividing the sum of grade points multiplied by credit hours of all semesters by total credit hours.

title: Rounding — Gpa
content: If the third decimal in GPA is 5 or more, it is rounded up.

title: Rounding — Gpa
content: If the third decimal in GPA is 4 or less, it is rounded down.

title: Withdrawn — Academic Rules
content: A withdrawn course is not counted as fail and is not included in GPA or CGPA calculation.

title: Incomplete — Academic Rules
content: An incomplete course is not included in GPA or CGPA calculation.

title: Evaluation — Thesis
content: Thesis or project evaluation is conducted by an external examiner appointed by the competent authority.

title: Viva — Thesis
content: The viva voce of thesis is conducted by the external examiner along with the supervisor and head of department.

title: Payment — Thesis
content: Honorarium is paid to examiners including the head of department for thesis evaluation.

title: University — Convocation Introduction
content: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University Peshawar (SBBWU) is the first women university of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It aims to empower female students through education, research, and development in scientific, socio-cultural, economic, and political fields.

title: Founder — Convocation History
content: The Convocation tradition at SBBWU was initiated under the leadership of the founding Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Syeda Farhana Jahangir, establishing it as an annual academic event.

title: First Convocation — Convocation Event
content: The first convocation was held on 28 March 2012 at the University of Peshawar Convocation Hall, where 213 graduates were awarded degrees.

title: Ms Degrees — Convocation Degrees
content: A total of 154 MS degrees were awarded in Psychology, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, and Statistics, while 59 MA degrees were awarded in Arabic, Islamiyat, and English.

title: Gold Medals — Convocation Awards
content: A total of 34 students received Gold Medals for their outstanding academic performance.

title: Chief Guest — Convocation Guests
content: The convocation was graced by Chancellor Barrister Syed Masood Kausar (Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) as chief guest, along with distinguished guests, students, and parents.

title: Speech — Convocation Speeches
content: The Chancellor appreciated the performance of students and congratulated faculty, graduates, and parents. The founding Vice Chancellor delivered the welcome address.

title: It Infrastructure — It Centre
content: Information Technology Centre (IT Centre) established in 2011 under Registrar Office to manage and support university IT infrastructure including computer networks, systems, UPS and power equipment, wireless hotspots, online databases, IP phones, video conferencing, university web portal, digital library, multimedia operations, CCTV surveillance, attendance & payroll system, campus wireless connectivity, HEC IT projects, IT procurement liaison, network maintenance, IT policy management, and IT skills development for staff and faculty.

title: Ict Services Overview — It Services
content: IT Centre provides ICT services for students and staff including computer labs, internet access, help desk support, video conferencing, learning center, internships, final year project support, IT career counselling, and ICT workshops.

title: Lab Facilities — Computer Labs
content: Computer labs provide hardware, software, and workspace access with technical staff support. Facilities include licensed software, internet/intranet access, printing, and photocopying services.

title: It Helpdesk — Support Services
content: IT Service Desk offers technical support for computers, laptops, mobile devices, home networking issues, and data recovery services along with computing guidance.

title: Support Contact — Contact Information
content: Support is available via email, phone, walk-in service at Data Centre, and official IT Centre website.

title: Training Programs — Learning Center
content: Learning Center provides training, consulting, multimedia production, graphics, photography, videography, and workshops on standard applications and systems.

title: Final Year Project Support — Academic Support
content: IT Centre supports final year projects, networking and hosting solutions, open-source software deployment, and provides internship opportunities and project-based honorary roles.

title: Itservice Availability — Operations
content: IT Centre operates 24/7 for services with staff deployment based on institutional needs and ongoing expansion.

title: It Complaint — Complaint Form
content: The IT Complaint Performa is an official form used to register IT-related issues at the IT Centre of the university. It allows students and staff to report technical problems such as computer faults, network issues, or IT service disruptions for resolution by the IT support team.
